Shlomo (Shlomi) Yirmiahu, son of Ruti and David, was born on Shabbat, 7 Sivan 5746 (14 June 1986), at Assaf Harofeh Hospital in Tzrifin. He was the eldest of four siblings, the brother of Ati, Netanel and Yehonatan. Shlomi grew up and was educated in the Ramat Eliyahu neighborhood of Rishon LeZion. He studied at the "Beit Efraim" elementary school and the Yitzhak Rabin middle school, and completed high school at "Makif Heh" (Makif Heh High School), where he was an outstanding student in his class.

From a young age he loved sport. At the age of eleven he joined the karate school of Sensei Arie Nicker, and at thirteen he already took part in a European karate competition in Sweden. Shlomi excelled in his studies and took part in many national karate competitions. He was only a short time away from earning his black belt.

Apart from karate, Shlomi developed a talent for computers, in which he excelled. He loved spending time with his friends at clubs and enjoying life.

Shlomi eagerly awaited his enlistment in the IDF; everyone knew he would be a combat soldier. On 28 November 2004 he enlisted, volunteered for the Armored Corps and served as a gunner. He loved his service and his corps and intended to reach the tank commanders' course. Although he suffered from back injuries that made things physically difficult for him, he firmly refused to hear of any option to change the nature of his service that might have separated him from his unit comrades and his military role.

Everyone knew Shlomi for the constant smile on his face. He was kind-hearted, modest and quiet, and even his close family was surprised, after his fall, to hear about the things he had done and the people he had helped.

In the Second Lebanon War, on 16 Tammuz 5766 (12 July 2006), Shlomi fell in battle in southern Lebanon. Early that morning Hizbullah launched a large-scale attack along the Lebanese border and abducted two reservists, Staff Sergeant Ehud Goldwasser and Sergeant First Class Eldad Regev. The outpost where Shlomi and his crew were stationed came under heavy artillery bombardment. When news of the abduction came, and as they were at the outpost closest to the site, the crew was ordered to enter Lebanon and stop the terrorists' escape vehicle. The crew struggled to reach the tank because of the heavy shelling, but through tremendous effort and determination they reached the tank and, together with an armored personnel carrier, began driving toward Lebanon. As they entered Lebanon, the crew managed to fire and hit several Hizbullah positions, but very close to the border, near the Hizbullah outpost of "Kipat HaDegel," the tank struck a large underside mine, which destroyed the tank and killed all four crew members on the spot, Shlomi among them. Falling with Shlomi were Sergeant First Class Yaniv Bar-On, Sergeant First Class Gadi Mosayev and Sergeant First Class Alex Kushnirsky.

On 14 July 2006, exactly one month after he celebrated his twentieth birthday, Shlomi was laid to rest in the military cemetery in Rishon LeZion. He left behind his parents, two brothers and a sister. His family inscribed on his tombstone: "We will always remember your smile; you will always be a hero."

Following his death, Shlomi was posthumously promoted to the rank of Sergeant First Class.
